name: roadmap.sh
why: Community-maintained skill maps for almost every developer role, with links per topic.
tip: Use it as a checklist, not a syllabus. Tick off topics only after you have used them in a project.

name: CS50x: Introduction to Computer Science
why: The best free first course in programming: C, Python, SQL and the web, with real problem sets.
tip: Do every problem set yourself before watching the walkthroughs. The final project is your first portfolio piece.

name: The Missing Semester
why: Shell, Git, editors, debugging and scripting: the tools colleges skip and jobs assume.
tip: Spend one evening per lecture and redo each exercise in your own terminal.

name: Pro Git
why: The official, free Git book. Chapters 2 and 3 cover what you need every day.
tip: Read chapters 2 and 3, then practise branching on Learn Git Branching.

name: Learn Git Branching
why: A visual sandbox that makes rebase, merge and cherry-pick finally make sense.
tip: Finish the Main and Remote levels. You will stop fearing merge conflicts.

name: The Odin Project
why: A full, project-based web curriculum that makes you set up real tools from day one.
tip: Follow the Full Stack JavaScript path and actually build every project. Ask for help in their Discord.

name: freeCodeCamp
why: Thousands of hours of free interactive lessons with free certifications built around projects.
tip: Use it for structured practice. The certification projects matter more than the certificates.

name: Build your own X
why: Step-by-step guides to rebuild real tools: Git, Redis, a database, a shell, an interpreter.
tip: Pick one tool you use daily and rebuild it. Few things teach more or look better on a CV.

name: Exercism
why: Free coding exercises in 70+ languages with optional human mentoring.
tip: Use it to pick up a second language fast. Request a mentor review on your solutions.

name: GitHub Student Developer Pack
why: Free credits and pro plans for dozens of developer tools if you are a student.
tip: Claim it on day one with your college email or ID. It includes domains, cloud credits and Copilot.

name: MDN Web Docs
why: The reference for HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Accurate, current and free.
tip: Search MDN before Stack Overflow. Its Learn section is a solid beginner course on its own.

name: The Modern JavaScript Tutorial
why: The clearest free explanation of JavaScript from basics to closures, promises and the event loop.
tip: Read part 1 in order and do the tasks at the end of each chapter.

name: Learn CSS, HTML and more
why: Short, current courses on CSS, accessibility, forms, images and performance.
tip: Do Learn CSS and Learn Accessibility. They fix most beginner layout and a11y mistakes.

name: React docs: Learn
why: The official React course with interactive sandboxes. Better than most paid courses.
tip: Read Thinking in React and Escape Hatches twice. Build the tic-tac-toe tutorial without copying.

name: Learn Next.js
why: Official hands-on course that builds a full dashboard app with routing, data and auth.
tip: Finish it, then rebuild the same app with your own design and data.

name: TypeScript Handbook
why: The official guide to TypeScript. Short enough to read in a weekend.
tip: Read Everyday Types and Narrowing, then turn on strict mode in your next project.

name: CSS for JavaScript Developers
why: The course that finally explains how CSS layout really works. Worth paying for.
tip: Buy it only after you have built two or three sites and keep fighting CSS.

name: Frontend Masters
why: Deep workshops by working engineers on JavaScript, React, performance and more.
tip: One month is enough to binge the two or three workshops you need. Check for student pricing.

name: Scrimba
why: Interactive screencasts where you pause the video and edit the code in place.
tip: Start with the free Learn JavaScript and Learn React courses.

name: Frontend Mentor
why: Real design files to turn into working pages, with community code reviews.
tip: Do one challenge a week. Pick ones with mobile and desktop designs and match them closely.

name: devChallenges
why: Project briefs for frontend, backend and full-stack apps with designs included.
tip: Use the full-stack challenges as portfolio projects once you know a framework.

name: Visual Studio Code
why: The default editor. Free, fast and has an extension for everything.
tip: Learn ten shortcuts (multi-cursor, go to definition, rename symbol). It saves hours every week.

name: Chrome DevTools docs
why: How to debug layout, network and performance problems like a professional.
tip: Learn the Performance and Network panels. Interviewers love candidates who can profile.

name: Figma
why: Where designs live. Developers need to read it even if they never design.
tip: Learn to inspect spacing, export assets and use Dev Mode. The free plan is enough.

name: Vercel
why: Deploy a frontend from GitHub in a minute with a free hobby plan.
tip: Every project you build should have a live link. Put it at the top of your README.

name: Kevin Powell
why: The friendliest CSS teacher online. Short, practical videos on layout and modern CSS.
tip: Watch his grid and flexbox videos when a layout fights you.

name: Web Dev Simplified
why: Clear, short explanations of JavaScript and React concepts.
tip: Search his channel for the exact concept you are stuck on.

name: Fireship
why: Fast, accurate overviews of tools and tech news in a few minutes.
tip: Use it to decide what to learn next, not to learn it. Follow up with the official docs.

name: Akshay Saini (Namaste JavaScript)
why: Deep JavaScript internals explained in a way Indian interview panels love.
tip: Watch the Namaste JavaScript playlist before frontend interviews.

name: Chai aur Code (Hitesh Choudhary)
why: Full projects and stacks taught in Hindi by a long-time industry engineer.
tip: Pick one full-stack project series and build it along with him, then change it.

name: Reactiflux
why: The largest React community on Discord, with help channels and job boards.
tip: Ask in the help channels with a minimal code example. You will get answers fast.

name: JavaScript Weekly
why: One email a week with the JavaScript news and articles worth reading.
tip: Skim the headlines, open two links. That is enough to stay current.

name: Bytes
why: A funny, short JavaScript newsletter twice a week.
tip: Good for staying aware of the ecosystem without doom-scrolling.

name: Syntax
why: Practical web development podcast with tasty tips you can use the same day.
tip: Listen on commutes. Note one thing to try per episode.

name: Node.js Learn
why: Official guides to Node.js: modules, async code, files, HTTP and testing.
tip: Build a tiny HTTP server without a framework first. Then frameworks make sense.

name: Django tutorial
why: The official step-by-step tutorial for Python's most complete web framework.
tip: Finish all eight parts, then build your own app with users and an admin.

name: FastAPI tutorial
why: Modern Python APIs with type hints and automatic docs. Popular with AI teams.
tip: Use it to serve your ML models and LLM apps behind a real API.

name: Spring guides
why: Short official guides for Spring Boot, still the most hired Java stack in India.
tip: Do Building a RESTful Web Service and Accessing Data with JPA first.

name: Karmatix .NET Academy
why: Our own free .NET 10 and C# 14 course with 16 tested projects and interview prep.
tip: Follow the modules in order and push every lab to your GitHub.

name: Microsoft Learn: .NET
why: Official free .NET learning paths with in-browser sandboxes.
tip: Use it alongside a project. The ASP.NET Core paths are the most useful.

name: A Tour of Go
why: Learn Go interactively in a few evenings. Go runs most cloud tooling.
tip: Finish the tour, then read Go by Example as your daily reference.

name: Go by Example
why: Annotated, runnable examples of every common Go task.
tip: Keep it open while you build your first CLI tool in Go.

name: PostgreSQL tutorial
why: The official introduction to the database most new projects choose.
tip: Install Postgres locally and do every query yourself.

name: SQLBolt
why: Interactive SQL lessons that take an afternoon and stick.
tip: Do all lessons in one sitting, then move to DataLemur for interview problems.

name: Use The Index, Luke
why: Why queries are slow and how indexes fix them. Rare, practical knowledge.
tip: Read it when your first app gets slow. It pays off in system design rounds.

name: System Design Primer
why: The classic free guide to scaling, caching, queues and databases.
tip: Read it alongside ByteByteGo videos. Practise by designing apps you use daily.

name: ByteByteGo
why: Animated system design explainers that are easy to remember in interviews.
tip: Watch one video a day for a month before system design rounds.

name: Hussein Nasser
why: Backend fundamentals explained deeply: databases, proxies, protocols.
tip: Pick topics you use at work or in projects and go deep.

name: Gaurav Sen
why: System design taught by an Indian engineer who popularised it for interviews.
tip: Watch his design walkthroughs, then try the same problem on paper first.

name: Piyush Garg
why: Node.js, system design and GenAI projects in Hindi with real deployments.
tip: Build his projects end to end, including the deployment parts.

name: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
why: The most respected book on how real systems store and move data.
tip: Read it after your first year of building. One chapter a week is plenty.

name: CodeCrafters
why: Build your own Redis, Git, HTTP server or SQLite with automated tests checking each stage.
tip: Do one challenge in the language you want a job in. Mention it in interviews.

name: Boot.dev
why: A gamified backend path in Python, Go and SQL with lots of coding.
tip: Content is free to read. Pay only if the interactive mode keeps you consistent.

name: Bruno
why: An open source API client that saves requests as files in your repo.
tip: Commit your API collection next to the code so reviewers can try your API.

name: Docker: Get started
why: Containers are expected in almost every backend and DevOps job now.
tip: Add a Dockerfile and a compose file to every backend project you build.

name: Redis University
why: Free official courses on caching, data structures and queues with Redis.
tip: Add caching to one of your APIs and measure the speedup.

name: Flutter docs
why: Official Flutter documentation with a great getting-started path and cookbook.
tip: Do the first app codelab, then use the Cookbook for every feature you need.

name: Karmatix Flutter Course
why: Our own free Flutter and Dart course with Kotlin comparisons and timed mock tests.
tip: Use the mock tests if you are preparing for company exams.

name: Android Basics with Compose
why: Google's free official course for native Android with Kotlin and Jetpack Compose.
tip: Finish all units and publish one app on the Play Store, even a small one.

name: Kotlin docs
why: Official Kotlin guide with a free Koans practice set.
tip: Do the Kotlin Koans before Android so the language is not in your way.

name: 100 Days of SwiftUI
why: The best free route into iOS development: one small lesson a day.
tip: Follow the days strictly. Consistency is the whole point of this course.

name: React Native and Expo docs
why: Build iOS and Android apps with React. Expo makes setup painless.
tip: If you already know React, this is the fastest way to ship a mobile app.

name: Firebase docs
why: Auth, database, storage and notifications without running a server.
tip: Use it for your first apps, then learn a real backend so you are not locked in.

name: Philipp Lackner
why: Practical Android and Kotlin videos on architecture, Compose and clean code.
tip: Watch his architecture series after your first working app.

name: Flutter (official channel)
why: Widget of the Week and official talks from the Flutter team.
tip: Watch Widget of the Week to learn widgets you did not know existed.

name: AWS Skill Builder
why: Official AWS training with free courses and exam prep, plus paid labs.
tip: Take the free Cloud Practitioner Essentials before any paid AWS course.

name: AWS Free Tier
why: Free usage of many AWS services to practise on a real account.
tip: Set a billing alarm at ₹100 on day one. Delete resources after every lab.

name: Microsoft Learn: Azure
why: Free official Azure paths with sandboxes, mapped to every Azure exam.
tip: Join a Microsoft Virtual Training Day for a chance at a discounted or free exam voucher.

name: Google Cloud Skills Boost
why: Hands-on Google Cloud labs in real temporary projects.
tip: Watch for free credit campaigns and do the skill badges, which show on your profile.

name: Kubernetes tutorials
why: Official tutorials that take you from a first deployment to stateful apps.
tip: Run them on a local cluster with kind or minikube, not just in your head.

name: Killercoda
why: Free browser-based Linux and Kubernetes playgrounds, including CKA practice scenarios.
tip: Use it daily before the CKA. It is the closest free thing to the real exam.

name: iximiuz Labs
why: Hands-on challenges for containers, Kubernetes and networking that explain how things work inside.
tip: Do the container challenges after Docker basics. You will understand what Docker really does.

name: KodeKloud
why: DevOps courses with built-in labs. Very popular for CKA and Terraform prep.
tip: The CKA course plus its mock exams is a common, proven combination.

name: Terraform tutorials
why: Official step-by-step tutorials for infrastructure as code.
tip: Rebuild your cloud resume project's infrastructure with Terraform.

name: Linux Upskill Challenge
why: A free month-long course where you run a real Linux server.
tip: Do it on a cheap or free cloud VM. Day by day, without skipping.

name: OverTheWire: Bandit
why: A game that teaches Linux commands by making you hack your way through levels.
tip: Do it before any security course. Write down how you solved each level.

name: 90DaysOfDevOps
why: A free, day-by-day DevOps learning plan written in public.
tip: Use it as a schedule and post your daily progress publicly.

name: The Cloud Resume Challenge
why: One project that touches DNS, storage, serverless, a database, CI/CD and IaC.
tip: The best single cloud portfolio project. Write a blog post about what broke.

name: DevOps Exercises
why: Hundreds of DevOps interview questions and exercises with answers.
tip: Use it in the last two weeks before interviews.

name: GitHub Actions docs
why: Free CI/CD built into GitHub. Every project should have a pipeline.
tip: Add tests and a deploy workflow to one project. Show the green badge in your README.

name: TechWorld with Nana
why: The clearest Docker, Kubernetes and DevOps tutorials on YouTube.
tip: Watch the full Kubernetes crash course, then do Killercoda scenarios.

name: Abhishek Veeramalla
why: Free DevOps zero to hero series by an Indian engineer, with real projects.
tip: Follow the series and push every project to GitHub.

name: Kubernetes Slack
why: Where Kubernetes maintainers and users talk. Great for contributing to open source.
tip: Join the SIG channels that interest you and start with good first issues.

name: Practical Deep Learning
why: Top-down deep learning: train real models in lesson one, theory later.
tip: Run every notebook yourself on Kaggle or Colab and change the dataset.

name: Machine Learning Specialization
why: Andrew Ng's updated classic. The best foundation in ML ideas.
tip: Audit or apply for Coursera financial aid. Do the labs, not just the videos.

name: DeepLearning.AI short courses
why: One to two hour free courses on LLM apps, agents, RAG and fine-tuning, often with the tool makers.
tip: Do one per week and turn each into a tiny project on GitHub.

name: Hugging Face Learn
why: Free courses on LLMs, agents, diffusion and more using open models.
tip: Do the LLM course and push a model or Space to your Hugging Face profile.

name: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero
why: Build a GPT from scratch with one of the best teachers in the field.
tip: Type the code yourself, do not copy it. This is how you understand LLMs.

name: 3Blue1Brown: Neural networks
why: Beautiful visual intuition for how neural networks and transformers work.
tip: Watch it before any deep learning course.

name: Kaggle Learn and competitions
why: Free micro-courses, datasets, free GPU notebooks and real competitions.
tip: Finish Intro to ML, then join a Getting Started competition and publish your notebook.

name: Machine Learning Crash Course
why: Google's fast-paced free ML introduction with interactive exercises.
tip: A good refresher before ML interviews.

name: OpenAI Cookbook
why: Working examples for building with LLM APIs: RAG, evals, tools and agents.
tip: Copy patterns, not code. Rebuild one example with a provider of your choice.

name: Anthropic courses
why: Free notebooks on prompt engineering, tool use and evaluations.
tip: Do the prompt engineering tutorial before you build your first LLM feature.

name: Made With ML
why: How to take ML from a notebook to production: testing, serving and monitoring.
tip: Use it after you can train a model. This is what ML engineering jobs ask for.

name: Ollama
why: Run open models on your own laptop with one command.
tip: Build a small local RAG app with it. No API bill while you learn.

name: Google Colab
why: Free Jupyter notebooks in the browser with GPU access.
tip: Use it for fast.ai and Kaggle work if your laptop has no GPU.

name: AI Engineering
why: The most practical book on building products with foundation models.
tip: Read the chapters on evaluation and RAG first.

name: Krish Naik
why: Free ML, deep learning and GenAI playlists from an Indian data scientist.
tip: Follow one complete playlist rather than random videos.

name: CampusX
why: Deep, structured ML and data science lessons in Hindi.
tip: The 100 Days of Machine Learning playlist is a complete course.

name: Latent Space
why: The podcast for AI engineers, with builders explaining what works in production.
tip: Listen to episodes on evals and agents before AI interviews.

name: The Batch
why: A weekly AI news letter from Andrew Ng's team, calm and accurate.
tip: Skim weekly to keep up without the hype.

name: Hugging Face Discord
why: Active community around open models, courses and study groups.
tip: Join the course channels while you take the Hugging Face courses.

name: Google Data Analytics Certificate
why: A structured beginner programme in spreadsheets, SQL, Tableau and R.
tip: Apply for Coursera financial aid if cost is a problem. Do the capstone on your own dataset.

name: DataLemur
why: Real SQL interview questions from tech companies, with a free tier.
tip: Do the free SQL questions in the two weeks before analyst interviews.

name: StrataScratch
why: SQL and Python interview questions taken from real company rounds.
tip: Filter by company to practise for a specific interview.

name: SQLZoo
why: Free interactive SQL tutorials and quizzes.
tip: Do the SELECT, JOIN and aggregate sections until they feel boring.

name: Microsoft Learn: Power BI
why: Free official Power BI paths. Power BI is the most asked BI tool in Indian job posts.
tip: Build one dashboard on public data and publish screenshots and a write-up.

name: Tableau Public
why: Free Tableau with a public profile that works as a portfolio.
tip: Publish three dashboards that each answer one clear question.

name: pandas: getting started
why: The official introduction to the library every analyst uses.
tip: Clean one messy public dataset end to end. That is the real skill.

name: Alex The Analyst
why: A free data analyst bootcamp on YouTube with SQL, Excel, Tableau and portfolio projects.
tip: Follow his portfolio project videos and build your own versions.

name: Luke Barousse
why: Data analyst skills backed by real job posting data.
tip: Use his videos to decide which tools to learn first.

name: DataTalks.Club
why: Free cohort-based zoomcamps for data engineering, ML and LLMs, plus a big Slack.
tip: Join the next free zoomcamp cohort. Deadlines keep you going.

name: dbt Learn
why: Free official courses for analytics engineering with SQL.
tip: Take dbt Fundamentals if you want analytics engineer roles.

name: NPTEL
why: Free IIT and IISc courses. The optional proctored exam gives a certificate many Indian employers recognise.
tip: Pick courses that match your path and take the exam for credit if your college accepts it.

name: LeetCode
why: The standard platform for coding interview practice.
tip: Do problems by pattern, not at random. Use the NeetCode list to stay focused.

name: NeetCode
why: A curated list of interview problems grouped by pattern, each with a video solution.
tip: Do NeetCode 150 in order. Try for 25 minutes before watching the solution.

name: Striver's A2Z DSA sheet
why: A complete DSA sheet from basics to advanced, built for Indian placements.
tip: Pick either this or NeetCode and finish it. Switching sheets is the common trap.

name: GeeksforGeeks
why: Articles, practice problems and company-wise interview experiences.
tip: Read company interview experiences before every on-campus test.

name: Codeforces
why: The main competitive programming platform with live contests.
tip: Join Div 3 and Div 2 contests every week. Upsolve one problem after each.

name: CodeChef
why: Indian competitive programming platform with weekly Starters contests.
tip: Good for beginners: start with Starters contests and the practice section.

name: CSES Problem Set
why: 300 classic problems that cover every core algorithm topic.
tip: Solve the sorting, DP and graph sections. They come up again and again.

name: VisuAlgo
why: Animations of data structures and algorithms step by step.
tip: Watch an algorithm here before you code it.

name: Tech Interview Handbook
why: Free guide to the full interview process: resume, coding, behavioural and negotiation.
tip: Read the resume and behavioural sections. Most candidates skip them.

name: Apna College
why: Popular beginner DSA and web courses in Hindi.
tip: Good first exposure in Hindi. Pair it with real practice on LeetCode or CodeChef.

name: CodeWithHarry
why: Long beginner courses in Hindi for Python, web development and more.
tip: Use one full course to start, then switch to building your own projects quickly.

name: Abdul Bari
why: Classic algorithms lectures that make the theory easy to follow.
tip: Watch his lectures for topics you keep getting wrong.

name: CodeHelp by Babbar
why: Full DSA course in C++ in Hindi, widely used for placements.
tip: Follow the DSA playlist with the matching sheet.

name: AmbitionBox
why: Salaries, reviews and interview questions for Indian companies.
tip: Read the interview section for each company before you apply.

name: Web Security Academy
why: The best free web security training, with hundreds of hands-on labs.
tip: Do the apprentice labs for every topic. Every backend developer should do the first ones.

name: TryHackMe
why: Guided, browser-based security rooms. The friendliest start in cybersecurity.
tip: Do the free Pre Security and Cyber Security 101 paths before paying.

name: Hack The Box Academy
why: Structured modules and real machines to hack. Respected by employers.
tip: Students get discounted access. Write up every retired machine you solve.

name: OWASP Top 10
why: The ten most important web application risks, from the main open security community.
tip: Learn each one well enough to explain it with an example in an interview.

name: picoCTF
why: Beginner-friendly capture the flag challenges that stay open all year.
tip: Use the practice gym to learn each category: web, crypto, forensics, binary.

name: Hacker101
why: Free video lessons and CTF for bug bounty hunting.
tip: Finish the CTF to get invites to private bug bounty programmes.

name: Professor Messer
why: Complete free video courses for CompTIA A+, Network+ and Security+.
tip: If you take Security+, his free course plus a practice test is enough for many people.

name: John Hammond
why: Malware analysis and CTF walkthroughs that show how experts think.
tip: Pause and try each step before he does.

name: NetworkChuck
why: Energetic networking, Linux and security projects you can do at home.
tip: Build one of his home lab projects. Great interview story.

name: CTFtime
why: The calendar of every CTF competition, with team rankings.
tip: Join or form a team and play one online CTF a month.

name: tl;dr sec
why: The best weekly security newsletter: tools, research and talks, summarised.
tip: Read it weekly to know what security teams are talking about.

name: Google Developer Groups
why: Free local meetups and DevFests in most Indian cities.
tip: Go to one event a month and talk to two people. Volunteer to get to know organisers.

name: AWS User Groups
why: Local AWS meetups and Community Days run by volunteers, many in India.
tip: Speak at a meetup after your first cloud project. It counts as experience.

name: FOSS United
why: India's open source community: city meetups, IndiaFOSS conference and grants.
tip: Attend your city's FOSS meetup and show something you built.

name: Hasgeek
why: Indian tech conferences and talks by practitioners, such as Rootconf.
tip: Watch past talks for free and attend one event in person when you can.

name: Commudle
why: Indian platform listing developer communities and events.
tip: Find active communities in your city or college here.

name: Major League Hacking
why: Student hackathons and a fellowship programme around the world, many online.
tip: Do one hackathon a quarter. Finish and present something, even if small.

name: Devfolio
why: Where most Indian hackathons happen, including ETHIndia and college hackathons.
tip: Keep your Devfolio profile filled with your projects. Judges check it.

name: Unstop
why: Competitions, hackathons, quizzes and internships from Indian companies and colleges.
tip: Company coding challenges here often lead directly to interviews.

name: Google Summer of Code
why: Paid, mentored open source work over the summer.
tip: Start contributing to an organisation two to three months before applications open.

name: LFX Mentorship
why: Paid mentorships on Linux Foundation and CNCF projects like Kubernetes.
tip: Pick a project you already use and make small contributions before applying.

name: Outreachy
why: Paid open source internships for people underrepresented in tech.
tip: Read the eligibility rules early. The contribution period decides selection.

name: GirlScript Summer of Code
why: A beginner-friendly open source programme run in India.
tip: A good first step before GSoC: learn how pull requests and reviews work.

name: Hacktoberfest
why: Every October, contribute to open source with thousands of others.
tip: Aim for meaningful pull requests, not typo fixes. Maintainers notice.

name: r/developersIndia
why: India's largest developer forum: jobs, salaries, interviews and advice.
tip: Search before you ask. The salary and interview threads are gold.

name: r/learnprogramming
why: A welcoming forum for beginner questions.
tip: Post your code and what you tried. Good questions get good answers.

name: DEV Community
why: Write and read developer posts. Writing about what you learn gets you noticed.
tip: Post a short write-up of every project you finish.

name: Stack Overflow
why: Still the biggest archive of answered programming questions.
tip: Answering questions in your stack is a great way to learn it deeply.

name: Meetup
why: Find local tech meetups in your city.
tip: Search your stack plus your city. Smaller meetups are easier to network at.

name: Peerlist
why: Developer profiles built from your GitHub and projects, popular in India.
tip: Use it as your public proof of work and launch projects there.

name: freeCodeCamp Forum
why: Friendly help forum for anyone learning to code.
tip: Ask project questions with a link to your code.

name: TLDR
why: Daily five-minute summaries of tech, AI and web development news.
tip: Subscribe to the one edition that matches your path.

name: ByteByteGo Newsletter
why: Weekly system design explainers with clear diagrams.
tip: Free issues are enough. Save the diagrams for interview revision.

name: The Pragmatic Engineer
why: How real tech companies work: careers, salaries, engineering culture.
tip: Read the free issues to understand what senior engineers care about.

name: The Changelog
why: Conversations with the people who build open source software.
tip: Pick episodes about tools you use.

name: Internshala
why: India's largest internship board for students and freshers.
tip: Apply to small companies with a tailored note and a project link.

name: Wellfound
why: Startup jobs with salary ranges shown upfront.
tip: Apply directly to founders with a short note on what you would build.

name: Instahyre
why: Indian job platform where companies reach out to you.
tip: Complete your profile with projects. Recruiters search by skills.

name: Cutshort
why: Indian tech hiring platform with skill-based matching.
tip: Keep your skills list honest. Matching works best that way.

name: Work at a Startup
why: Jobs at Y Combinator startups, including many in India.
tip: One profile reaches hundreds of funded startups.

name: Dart language tour
why: The official tour of Dart: types, null safety, classes, async and records.
tip: Read it with DartPad open and run every snippet.

name: DartPad
why: Run Dart and Flutter in the browser with nothing installed.
tip: Use it to try a widget or a language feature in seconds.

name: pub.dev
why: The package registry for Dart and Flutter, with scores and popularity.
tip: Prefer packages with Flutter Favorite badges, recent updates and high pub points.

name: Flutter codelabs
why: Guided, hands-on Flutter tutorials that end in a working app.
tip: Do Your first Flutter app, then the layout and animation codelabs.

name: Riverpod docs
why: A widely used state management and caching library for Flutter.
tip: Learn it after setState and Provider make sense. Do not start with it.

name: Bloc library docs
why: Event-driven state management that many Indian product companies ask for.
tip: Do the counter and weather tutorials. Know when Cubit is enough.

name: r/FlutterDev
why: The largest Flutter discussion forum: news, packages and help.
tip: Search before asking. Share your finished app for feedback.

name: C# documentation
why: The official C# guide from basics to the newest language features.
tip: Read the Tour of C#, then look up each feature as you use it.

name: ASP.NET Core docs
why: Official docs for web APIs, minimal APIs, auth, middleware and hosting.
tip: Build the minimal API tutorial, then read Fundamentals end to end.

name: Entity Framework Core docs
why: The official guide to EF Core: modelling, migrations, queries and performance.
tip: Read Performance and Querying before your first production app.

name: Nick Chapsas
why: Short, sharp videos on modern C# and .NET features and performance.
tip: Watch for new language features and benchmark-backed advice.

name: Milan Jovanovic
why: Clean architecture, EF Core and ASP.NET Core patterns with real code.
tip: Use his videos when you structure your capstone API.

name: dotnet (official channel)
why: Official .NET channel with release talks, .NET Conf and beginner series.
tip: Watch the beginner series for C# and the .NET Conf keynote each November.

name: TanStack Query docs
why: The standard way to fetch, cache and sync server data in React apps.
tip: Replace your useEffect data fetching with it in one project.

name: Testing Library
why: Test components the way users use them, not by implementation details.
tip: Write tests for one form and one list in your React app.

name: Vitest
why: Fast unit testing for Vite and modern JavaScript projects.
tip: Add it to your project and run tests in CI on every push.

name: Express
why: The minimal Node.js web framework most tutorials and older codebases use.
tip: Build one API with it so you understand middleware and routing.

name: NestJS docs
why: A structured Node.js framework with modules and dependency injection, popular in companies.
tip: Use it for your second API once Express feels limiting.

name: Prisma docs
why: A type-safe ORM for Node.js and TypeScript with migrations.
tip: Model your schema, run migrations and read the query performance guide.

name: The Python Tutorial
why: The official Python tutorial. Short, accurate and always up to date.
tip: Read sections 1 to 9 and type every example.

name: CS50P: Programming with Python
why: A free Python course with tests, libraries and a final project.
tip: Do every problem set. Use the final project as a portfolio piece.

name: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python
why: Practical Python for real tasks: files, spreadsheets, web scraping and email.
tip: Automate one real chore from your college or job with it.

name: pytest
why: The standard testing tool for Python.
tip: Write tests for your API and run them in GitHub Actions.

name: Real Python
why: Well-written tutorials on almost every Python topic.
tip: Search it whenever the official docs feel too dry.

name: dev.java: Learn
why: The official modern Java tutorials, covering records, streams and the latest language features.
tip: Learn modern Java here, not from old tutorials that stop at Java 8.

name: Java Programming MOOC
why: A free university Java course with hundreds of auto-graded exercises.
tip: Finish parts 1 to 7. The exercises build real fluency.

name: Spring Boot reference
why: The official reference for configuration, data, security and production features.
tip: Read the Actuator and configuration chapters before deploying.

name: Baeldung
why: Focused Java and Spring tutorials for almost every task.
tip: Search it for specific Spring problems while you build.

name: Guide to app architecture
why: Google's official guidance on layers, state and data flow in Android apps.
tip: Read it before your second app and refactor your first one.

name: Now in Android
why: Google's reference app showing modern Android architecture, Compose and testing.
tip: Clone it and trace one feature from the UI to the data layer.

name: React Native docs
why: The core React Native docs: components, platform APIs and performance.
tip: Read the Core Components and Performance sections alongside Expo.

name: Effective Go
why: How to write idiomatic Go, straight from the Go team.
tip: Read it after the tour, then review your own code against it.

name: Let's Go
why: A step-by-step book that builds a full production-style web app in Go.
tip: Worth buying if you want a Go backend job. Build along, chapter by chapter.
